children: A group of 17 Democratic senators is urging President Donald Trump to discuss an agreement with Chinese President Xi Jinping to slow or pause development of advanced artificial intelligence systems.
The senators sent Trump a letter Wednesday ahead of his planned meeting with Xi, according to Politico. The letter was led by Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland.

“As you prepare for the upcoming summit, we urge you to engage with President Xi directly to discuss efforts to avoid the potential harms of this technology for the safety and benefit of the world,” the letter said.
The senators said the United States and China should work toward an agreement covering the development of advanced AI systems.

“America leads in AI innovation, and we must lead the world in AI safety and international cooperation, including by working with China to develop a formal agreement that would slow down, and potentially enact a mutual pause in, frontier AI development,” the letter said.
The push comes as U.S. officials and technology leaders debate how to manage the risks from increasingly capable AI systems.
Trump said Tuesday that the United States should not limit AI development and rejected the idea of a global body governing the technology.

“We’re leading now over China by a lot and everyone else, and we’re going to keep it that way. We’re going to keep it very, very straight and very strong. I’m not going to stifle growth of anything that’s going to be bigger than the Industrial Revolution,” Trump said.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has proposed a “notification mechanism” between the United States and China for discussing AI-related incidents.
